subsystems.name: Optical display engine
subsystems.role: projects a focused image into the wearer's eye so it appears overlaid on the real world.

subsystems.name: Sensing suite
subsystems.role: captures the scene and the wearer's motion and voice for the AI to interpret.

subsystems.name: Compute and AI runtime
subsystems.role: runs vision, translation and language models, either on the glasses or on a paired phone or cloud service.

subsystems.name: Audio interface
subsystems.role: delivers spoken translations, navigation cues and assistant replies without blocking the ears.

subsystems.name: Power system
subsystems.role: supplies enough energy for a day of mixed use while staying light.

subsystems.name: Frame and thermal management
subsystems.role: houses all components in a comfortable, glasses-like form and spreads heat away from the head.

subsystems.name: Connectivity
subsystems.role: links the glasses to a phone, the internet and other devices.
parts: optional cellular modem on a paired device

buildSteps.title: Design the optical stack
buildSteps.detail: Choose a micro-display and a waveguide geometry, then simulate how light will travel from the display to the eye without ghosting or colour smearing.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate waveguides
buildSteps.detail: High-index glass wafers are patterned with surface-relief gratings using nano-imprint or etching, then diced and polished.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture micro-displays
buildSteps.detail: OLED or microLED arrays are built on silicon backplanes, with pixel sizes measured in a few micrometres.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the optical module
buildSteps.detail: The display, collimating lenses and waveguide are aligned to within a micrometre and fixed in place.

buildSteps.title: Build the electronics
buildSteps.detail: The system-on-chip, sensors, battery and antennas are placed into the temple arms, often on flexible printed circuits.

buildSteps.title: Train and optimise AI models
buildSteps.detail: Translation, object recognition and navigation models are trained, then compressed and quantised so they run on low power or a nearby phone.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Cameras are aligned with the display, the inertial unit is calibrated, and software is tuned so virtual objects stay anchored to the world.

buildSteps.title: Test and certify
buildSteps.detail: Units undergo drop, sweat, battery, electromagnetic and eye-safety testing before they can be sold.

buildSteps.title: Scale manufacturing
buildSteps.detail: Assembly and optical alignment are automated, and test lines are built to keep yields high.

prerequisites.why: microLED offers brightness and efficiency but is not yet cheap or high-resolution enough for mass-market glasses.
mass-producing waveguides with uniform colour and low light loss remains difficult and costly.
dedicated neural accelerators can run vision and speech models within a few watts.
translation, object detection and navigation are mature enough for real-time use.
current lithium-polymer cells limit all-day use in a lightweight frame.
Bluetooth and Wi-Fi reliably link glasses to a phone or cloud service.

pathway.milestone: audio-only AI glasses and monocular display glasses for notifications and basic translation
pathway.unlocks: hands-free access to an AI assistant and simple text prompts.

pathway.milestone: full-colour, high-brightness microLED displays with waveguides and on-device AI
pathway.unlocks: clear, contextual overlays for navigation and object recognition without a phone.

pathway.milestone: seamless augmented reality with SLAM, 3D mapping and persistent virtual objects
pathway.unlocks: navigation arrows that stick to the street and labels that stay on real objects.

pathway.milestone: always-on, prescription-ready glasses with all-day battery and optional cellular
pathway.unlocks: a true everyday wearable that replaces the phone for many tasks.
